chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Whoever plants a tree, or digs a valley from the beginning, with no one else having preceded him, and revives dead land, then it is for him, as a decree from Allah and His Messenger (peace be upon him and his family).'
ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic legal conditions for owning revived dead land?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi codifies the principle of 'Ihya al-Mawat' (reviving dead land), establishing that exclusive ownership is granted to the pioneer who cultivates unused land without prior claim, a ruling derived directly as a divine decree from Allah and His Messenger. In Shia jurisprudence, this serves as a foundational evidence for property rights based on labor and improvement, encouraging agricultural productivity and economic development by ensuring the cultivator retains the fruits of their effort.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The one who plants a tree, or digs out a valley beginning, no one else having preceded him, and revives a dead land, so it is for him, being a judgement from Allah<sup>ajwj</sup> and His<sup>ajwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from af-Nawfaliy from af-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘

Whoever plants a tree or digs a valley as the first one before anyone else and revives a land which is barren (dead), it becomes his land from Allah and the Messenger of Allah, ‘O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause.’”
